transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's really frustrating. Especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle paperwork or, you know, go over shared household plans. 

Like the other night, we were supposed to sit down and figure out the budget for fixing up the back deck. The wood out there is completely rotting, so I was looking into that composite decking? It's so incredibly expensive now, but I spent hours looking at it and I found this one color called 'Tiki Torch' that I actually really liked. My husband thinks it's way too orange, though, and he wanted to look at the actual numbers. But anyway, he had all the spreadsheets out at the kitchen table, and I just... I couldn't just sit there in the chair with him. I had to keep getting up, wiping down the counters, checking the front porch even though it was dark out... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just can't seem to sit still for that kind of stuff.
Have these difficulties with restlessness and sitting still been present since you were a child, or is this a more recent change for you?

Oh, no, it's definitely not a new thing. Looking back, this was already totally part of me in elementary school. I was always that girl with the completely messy desk. Actually, I remember in third grade, Mrs. Higgins—she was this really strict teacher who wore these huge, thick glasses—she made me dump my entire desk out in front of the whole class because I couldn't find my permission slip for the zoo field trip. I was always forgetting permission slips. 

And there were constantly notes going home to my parents saying I talked out of turn or that I just couldn't stay seated during lessons. Which is funny because at that zoo trip, I finally found the slip by the way, I remember seeing the penguins and they had this whole indoor enclosure that smelled absolutely terrible, like old fish and ammonia... I can still smell it if I think about it, it was so bad. We had to eat our packed lunches right after that, and I had a bologna sandwich that got completely ruined for me because of the smell. I haven't eaten bologna since. 

Um... wait, did you ask about my parents or just if it started when I was young? Just when I was young, right. Yeah, it's been happening since elementary school for sure.

{"intent": "Assess the presence of current inattention symptoms, specifically daily forgetfulness", "question": "In your day-to-day life now, how often do you find yourself forgetting routine responsibilities, like paying bills, keeping appointments,

Oh, all the time. It's actually a huge problem. I keep meaning to do things like return phone calls or pay a bill, and I'll tell myself, "Okay, I'm going to do that right after lunch." But then lunch happens, and I usually make a salad. I've been trying to eat healthier lately, so I started buying those pre-washed spring mixes in the plastic tubs? But they always go bad so fast. You open them once, and two days later it's just this slimy, green sludge at the bottom. I read somewhere that if you put a paper towel in the tub, it absorbs the moisture and keeps it fresh longer. I tried it, and it actually works pretty well! Though last week I bought spinach instead, and I completely forgot about it in the crisper drawer until it was practically liquid. 

But anyway, yeah, days will go by, and I'll realize I never made that call or paid that bill. Or I'll be supposed to bring something to a meeting—well, the PTA meetings, since I'm not working right now—and I'll literally be in the car, halfway to the school, before I remember that I left the sign-up sheets sitting right on the kitchen counter. So, yeah, forgetting things is definitely a daily struggle for me.

{"intent": "Screen for bipolar disorder by assessing for episodic periods of decreased need for sleep and elevated energy", "question": "Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you

Um, distinct periods? Like... no, I don't think so. I mean, my sleep is always kind of a mess anyway. Sometimes I'll stay up super late because I get caught up in something, like last week I started organizing my digital photos. I had thousands of them just sitting on my phone, and I realized I hadn't backed them up in years. I got this new external hard drive—it's one of those tiny solid-state ones, so small you could lose it in your purse. Which I actually did for a day, I panicked thinking I lost all the kids' baby pictures. But I found it at the bottom of my bag under a bunch of old receipts. The receipts are a whole other problem, they use that thermal paper that fades, so half of them are just blank strips of paper now anyway. 

But no, I don't have days where I just don't need sleep and feel super energized. I always feel like I need sleep, I'm just bad at actually getting to bed.

{"intent": "Differentiate ADHD from generalized anxiety disorder by assessing for chronic, uncontrollable worry across various topics", "question": "Do you find yourself struggling with excessive, hard

Excessive, hard-to-control worry? Um, I wouldn't say I worry about everything all the time. I mean, I stress about things when I mess up, like forgetting the PTA sign-up sheets, but it's not like I'm just sitting around worrying about the world ending or getting sick or whatever. 

Actually, speaking of getting sick, my youngest had this awful cough last month. It sounded like a seal barking, it was terrible. I took him to the pediatrician, Dr. Miller—he's great, he always wears these really loud, novelty ties. Last time he had one with little cartoon tacos all over it. Anyway, he said it was just croup and told us to run the shower really hot and sit in the bathroom with the steam. We did that, and it ruined the paint on the ceiling above the shower. It started bubbling and peeling off in these big, latex-y strips. My husband was so annoyed because he just painted that bathroom last spring. He used this color called "Sea Salt" which looked gray on the swatch but turned out looking really mint green once it was on the walls. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really have that chronic worry thing, unless there's an actual reason I messed something up.

Oh, waiting my turn? Yeah, that's... that's really hard for me. I just get really fidgety, and I catch myself checking my watch or my phone over and over again. 

Speaking of the pharmacy, I had to go there twice last week because they messed up my husband's prescription. He takes this cholesterol medication, and they gave him the wrong dosage. It was a whole thing. The pharmacist, Brenda—she's usually so on top of things, but she just got a new puppy. A golden retriever mix, I think? She was showing me pictures on her phone while I was waiting, and it was adorable. It had one blue eye and one brown eye. I guess that's called heterochromia? I read an article about that once. It happens in humans too, like that actor... oh, what's his name? The one from those old western movies. Anyway, the puppy was chewing on everything, and Brenda said it completely destroyed her favorite pair of slippers. I used to have a pair like that, but my neighbor's cat sprayed on them when I left them on the porch. 

But yeah, waiting in line or waiting to talk? It's just... I can't stand it. I get all antsy and just want it to be over.
